root_cause: CRLF / HTTP response-header injection / response splitting (CWE-113)

v0.ref: docker ruby:2.5.0-slim (bundled webrick, send_header has NO check_header)

v1.ref: docker ruby:2.5.1-slim (CVE-2017-17742 fix, MRI r62968 / webrick 7018305; check_header =~ /\r\n/)

flag.resource: response-header-stream integrity: a split-off header line the app never structurally emitted
flag.placement: per-run token embedded by the PoC into the CR/LF payload; materialises in the raw response ONLY when WEBrick's check_header ACCEPTS the control-char-bearing X-Reflected value and writes it to the socket
flag.detect: flag token substring in the raw HTTP response bytes (server response surface only; request path excluded)

mechanism.original_sink: regular response header (WEBrick app sets res['X-Reflected']=input)
mechanism.guard_line_v1: def check_header(header_value); if header_value =~ /\r\n/; raise InvalidHeader; else header_value; end; end
mechanism.guard_line_v2: def check_header(header_value); header_value = header_value.to_s; if /[\r\n]/ =~ header_value; raise InvalidHeader; else header_value; end; end

evidence.fix_reference: docker ruby:2.5.1-slim (CVE-2017-17742 fix, MRI r62968 / webrick 7018305; check_header =~ /\r\n/); docker ruby:2.5.8-slim (CVE-2019-16254 fix, webrick 8658b1b; check_header /[\r\n]/)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: This is the same issue as CVE-2017-17742. The previous fix was incomplete, which addressed the CRLF vector, but did not address an isolated CR or an isolated LF.
